A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same simulator and research work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. V1 includes supplementary Sections 6–9; v2 has no appended supplement but reworks some corresponding experiments into its main text. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, ImageNet classification, optical simulation, hardware validation, and supplementary freeform surface-recovery results.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction, simulator benchmarking, hardware comparisons, Fizeau interferometry, and freeform optimization results.

M1.justification: The core ray-wave renderer and PSF interpolation remain unchanged. The reported reconstruction objective changes its MSE term to RMSE while retaining perceptual loss. V2 Section 4.6 also specifies an adaptation that coherently accumulates wavelets across scene points for interferometry; freeform optimization itself already existed in v1.

E1.justification: DIV2K reconstruction remains, but v1's ten-class ImageNet classification task is removed. V2 adds Fizeau surface recovery and extends optical test conditions to 35°/40° off-axis PSFs. The existing freeform study is reworked from reference-height-map recovery into target-pattern design.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 6 introduces evaluated comparisons with Zemax-FFT, the Airy disk, Yang et al.'s ray-wave model, Wei et al., and Chen et al., using Zemax-Huygens as reference. These renderer comparisons were absent from v1. V2 Figure 11 also adds a ray-trained comparator to the freeform experiment.

E3.justification: The main reconstruction evaluation replaces the triplet pixel-size sweep with a singlet/triplet/six-aspheric lens grid and replaces curvature cosine similarity with RRMSE. V1's training-versus-dense-testing interpolation study is removed; its supplementary measurement-RMSE evaluation becomes a FoV-stratified SSIM study retaining the 969-PSF reference. V2 also introduces a renderer accuracy, ray-count, and runtime benchmark.

E4.justification: V2 adds comparative defocus/high-angle stress tests and a natural-versus-sparse-image spectral analysis, and revises interpolation sensitivity analysis across FoVs and lens complexities. V1's Grad-CAM++ analysis, pixel-size PSF study, F-number training trajectories, wave/ray forward-backward timing curves, and mesh-versus-B-spline ablation are absent.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, reproducibility seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained Monte Carlo ray sampling does not constitute new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 reports triplet wave/ray RMSE of 0.02040/0.02406 at 0.1 mm aperture and 1 micrometer pixels; v2 Table 1 reports 0.106/0.148 for its 0.1 mm triplet comparison. Reported objectives and settings differ, preventing matched-setting gain/loss claims. V2 adds renderer and application results and hardware SSIM of 0.781/0.853 on/off axis, while classification and several appendix result series disappear.

T1.justification: The optical-path-length, Rayleigh-Sommerfeld PSF, and isoplanatic interpolation equations (1–7), assumptions, and derivation are retained. The added implementation and application explanations introduce no new formal theorem, proof, or analytical derivation.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds reconstruction and classification gains, including the 16%/23% headline claims, and sensitivity to small pixels. V2 removes classification and those quantified headline claims, retains the importance of diffraction-aware optimization, and makes interferometric/freeform applicability a main contribution. This substantially changes the claimed scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of defocus-related sampling failures and why diffraction differences matter less for aberration-limited natural images than for high-frequency inputs. New Section 4.7 identifies limitations from strong aberrations and poorly defined focal/pupil geometry, including reference-sphere sampling problems. V1's pixel-size and classification feature-extraction interpretations are omitted.

D1.justification: V2 replaces a planned code release with a reported public repository and newly documents vectorization, PyTorch checkpointing, paraxial exit-pupil estimation, and sensor resizing to maintain FoV. Hardware wavelength and incidence angles become explicit. Conversely, v1's triplet glass identities and freeform B-spline implementation details are not retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially repositions the work around competing simulators' defocus accuracy, sampling costs, and differentiability. V2 adds field-tracing, generalized-Debye, and interferometry references while removing classification-related citations and DiffuserCam. Yang's preprint-to-conference bibliographic update represents the same prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. The classification section and separate supplementary structure disappear; freeform work is reworked into an Applications subsection, and Limitations is added. Retained method explanations and captions also receive substantial editing.

P2.justification: V2 adds a first-page results illustration, a multi-renderer PSF matrix, spectral analysis, and Fizeau/freeform panels. It redraws the lens comparison as an overlay and restructures the experimental tables. Classification heatmaps and many supplementary displays disappear; core method diagrams and hardware PSF panels are largely retained with revised placement and captions.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses a central validation gap: v1's simulator-accuracy claim relied mainly on qualitative PSFs and hardware agreement, whereas v2 Figure 6 provides quantitative fidelity and cost comparisons against multiple renderers, and Section 4.5 quantifies hardware agreement. The spectral analysis and explicit limitations also clarify applicability. Although classification and several training-level diagnostics are lost, the later version substantially strengthens support for its central physical-modeling claims.
